traps.title: The engine knew an order wouldn't fill
traps.plain: It checked the future to see an order expire, then took a later setup instead. That alone made a fake t of 5.74.

traps.title: Losing trades quietly deleted
traps.plain: Trades where the stop was hit on the entry bar were dropped. They were real losses.

traps.title: Profit counted before the trade existed
traps.plain: The bar's high may have printed before the order filled. Only the stop may count on that bar.

traps.title: Filled just by touching the price
traps.plain: A limit order isn't filled because the price touched it. Require the price to trade through by one tick.

traps.title: A stop on the wrong side of the entry
traps.plain: The engine booked wins that could not lose. It now crashes if this ever happens.

traps.title: Checking the stop before the trade opened
traps.plain: The exit logic started at the session open instead of the entry, so it tested prices from before the trade.

traps.title: Two price series lined up by row number
traps.plain: Row 500 of one file isn't the same day as row 500 of another. Always join on dates.

traps.title: A control built by flipping a net result
traps.plain: Negating a result after costs turns the cost into a gain.

traps.title: Costs charged wrongly
traps.plain: The wrong instrument's cost, costs left out of a 'net' number, or the same cost charged thousands of times.

traps.title: Interest counted as edge
traps.plain: ETF returns include coupon interest that a futures trader never earns. Strip it out before comparing.

traps.title: A 'hedged pair' that was one position
traps.plain: 99% of the money sat in one leg, so the 'edge' was just the interest rate.

traps.title: A date filter with a hole in it
traps.plain: Keeping only days 24–31 and 1–4 quietly built four-week trades out of three-day ones.

traps.title: Time zones
traps.plain: Minute data came in UTC. Convert once, with daylight saving, and check it against a known event.

traps.title: An income average that flattered everything
traps.plain: Dividing each path's payouts by its own lifetime inflated income tenfold. Use total paid over total months.

traps.title: A rule that moved with the thing being tested
traps.plain: The simulated payout gate changed with the setting being tested, so the comparison was rigged.

traps.title: Mixing months that happen together
traps.plain: Legs that move together must be drawn from the same month, or the risk looks smaller than it is.

traps.title: Several accounts treated as independent
traps.plain: One signal feeds them all, so they win and lose together.

traps.title: Positive in one unit, negative in another
traps.plain: A trade can make money per dollar traded and lose money per dollar risked. Report both.

traps.title: Closing prices hide the worst moment
traps.plain: An account is closed out by the worst price during the day, not the closing price.

traps.title: Assuming you can always try again
traps.plain: With one fee and one account, a blow-up is final. Plan for the first attempt.

traps.title: A safer sizing rule that never got paid
traps.plain: It cut blow-ups but stalled below the payout line.

traps.title: Labels swapped
traps.plain: Gross and net, harsh and lenient were mixed up at least once. Check every label.

traps.title: Review sites were wrong
traps.plain: Only a firm's own written answer counts.

traps.title: AI research reports mixed real sources with wrong numbers
traps.plain: Every figure has to be checked at the original source.

traps.title: An unfinished month counted as a month end
traps.plain: The last day in the data was treated as the month's last day, adding a trade that never happened.

traps.title: Returns added instead of compounded
traps.plain: A tick up and back down counted as a small win. Compound returns over the window.

traps.title: The pass check ignored the sign
traps.plain: It checked the size of t, not its direction, so a trade losing money at t −5.95 passed.

traps.title: Only today's survivors
traps.plain: A stock list built from companies alive today leaves out every company that went bust.

traps.title: Losers that silently vanish
traps.plain: When a stock is delisted its price series just stops. Book the final loss.

traps.title: Using a report before it was published
traps.plain: A December annual report is public in February or March. Use the filing date.

traps.title: Using corrected numbers nobody had at the time
traps.plain: Use the numbers as first reported, not later corrections.

traps.title: Insider trades dated too early
traps.plain: Insiders report days after they trade. The signal date is the filing date.

traps.title: Earnings released after the close
traps.plain: Day 0 is the first session the news could actually be traded.

traps.title: Tickers get reused
traps.plain: The same ticker can belong to different companies over time. Track companies by their SEC ID.

traps.title: Mixing adjusted and unadjusted prices
traps.plain: Dividing a split-adjusted price by unadjusted earnings gives nonsense ratios.

traps.title: Counting correlated trades as independent
traps.plain: Stocks held in the same month move together. Measure t on the monthly portfolio.

traps.title: The penny-stock bounce
traps.plain: Tiny prices bounce between bid and ask. Use a $1 floor and buy at the next close.

traps.title: Papers profit from the short side
traps.plain: Much of a published result comes from shorting. A long-only account can't collect that part.

traps.title: 500 stocks on paper, 10 in real life
traps.plain: Test the portfolio a small account can actually hold, with its costs.

traps.title: The wrong yardstick
traps.plain: Compare small stocks with small stocks, not with the S&P 500.

traps.title: Tuning the book's rules
traps.plain: Graham's numbers are tested as written. Any tuning counts as a new idea.

traps.title: Currency
traps.plain: The account is in euros and the stocks are in dollars. Count the exchange fees.

traps.title: Days with no trading
traps.plain: A day with zero volume shows a fake flat return. Require real trading on entry and exit days.

traps.title: A bad decade for the idea
traps.plain: The free data starts in value investing's worst decade. Say so, but don't lower the bar.

traps.title: Companies filed under their last ticker
traps.plain: WaMu's NYSE history sat under its later OTC ticker. Never filter the download by exchange.

traps.title: The same stock twice
traps.plain: One history under two codes. Detect it by identical returns, not by name.

traps.title: Glued-together price histories
traps.plain: A +144,000% day and a $1,000,000 placeholder price. Every move beyond ×3 in a day gets explained first.

traps.title: A typo worth trillions
traps.plain: Seagate was listed with 317 trillion shares. Check company size against a second source.

traps.title: Timestamps in the wrong time zone
traps.plain: Some SEC filing times marked UTC weren't UTC.

traps.title: Foreign listings in a US filter
traps.plain: A filter for US company listings also caught foreign ones.

traps.title: One bad stock skews the index
traps.plain: When a size-weighted check disagrees, look at the biggest contributors first.

traps.title: An invisible character broke a search
traps.plain: An automated edit wrote a hidden backspace into code, so a search silently matched nothing.

traps.title: A placebo that peeked
traps.plain: The fake dates were picked next to future earnings jumps, so the placebo looked like a discovery.
